maya: Quick sync  I'm opening a small refresh for the GreetKit quickstart. Goals: swap auth examples to ephemeral-token flow, add a tiny docker-compose for first deploy, and make model selection explicit. Draft PR in ~20m. Anyone take snippets?

jonah: I can check the auth code tonight. Which SDK?

maya: @redwood/inference v1.10.0 to use client.auth helpers.

liz: Link-checker flagged the env var doc link as 404 in the current doc. docs-bot posted it earlier.

docs-bot: automated-check: broken-link => https://old.docs.redwood.inference/auth/env-vars (404)

paul: For compose, keep it minimal: single node service running npm install && npm start, mount repo. Avoid DB bits.

maya: Noted. Also add a Mac M1 note to use node:18-bullseye-slim. Will add CI matrix for node 18/20.

jonah: Paste the signing snippet you plan to use so I can validate headers.

maya: draft snippet: export RW_API_KEY=sk.test_xxx
import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_API_KEY })
const token = await client.auth.getEphemeralToken({ ttlSeconds: 300 })
// use token for client calls

liz: tiny nit: mention refresh before reuse and param name ttlSeconds.

paul: compose example suggestion:
version: '3.8'
services:
  greetkit:
    image: node:18-bullseye-slim
    workdir: /app
    volumes: [.:/app]
    command: sh -c "npm install && npm run start"
    environment: [RW_API_KEY=${RW_API_KEY}]

maya: I'll open draft PR and tag reviewers: liz (copy/links), jonah (auth), paul (compose). Will add a short migration note about moving from static keys to ephemeral tokens.
